title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. It is a typed page (p. 114, Exposé IX) of Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §9 on 'extensions panachées' (mixed extensions). It sits in the archive folder between handwritten pages on C^{DR,pd}, and the archival stamp reads 432.

Setting: S is a henselian (reducible to strictly local) trait with generic point η, K its fraction field and V its valuation ring. A mixed extension X has a multiplicative part P, a middle term and an étale part Q, so that X is the given 'panachée' structure.

The page finishes the proof of Theorem 9.4.7:

(b) Uniqueness. The comparison map on Ext/torsor data from S to η is injective. This rests on the split exact sequence 0→V*→K*→Z→0 (the valuation). By the sorite 9.3, if X_η ≅ Y_η then X ≅ Y. Combined with (a), faithfulness, this gives that X ↦ X_η is fully faithful.

(c) Extension criterion. A mixed extension X_η over η extends to S if and only if the pairings (9.4.6.2) vanish. These are the pairings between the character/cocharacter data of the multiplicative and étale parts with values in K*/V* ≅ Z, i.e. the obstruction measured by valuations. Proof: uniqueness makes the question étale-local, so one reduces to S strictly local, where the statement holds by the construction preceding 9.4.6.

Section 9.5 then starts the ℓ-adic analogue. Fix a prime ℓ and pro-ℓ Barsotti–Tate groups P, R, Q, given as projective systems (X(n))_{n≥0} of Λ_n-modules with Λ_n = Z/ℓ^{n+1}. Take extensions 0→P→F→R→0 and 0→R→E→Q→0, levelwise (9.5.3), with Q étale and P multiplicative. This is the setup for the ℓ-adic monodromy pairing and the Galois-module description of mixed extensions, i.e. the ℓ-adic version of the semistable-reduction / monodromy filtration analysis in SGA 7 IX.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The phrasing 'qui est injective ... donc elle est injective' is slightly redundant: the second 'elle' refers to the original comparison map, deduced from the injectivity of the auxiliary map. This is in the original typescript.

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of restriction to the generic fibre for mixed extensions (multiplicative/étale) over a henselian trait, via split 0→V*→K*→Z→0
ideas.modern_name: Extension of mixed extensions / 1-motive-type degenerations; Néron-model extension property
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exp. IX (1967-69, publ. 1972)

ideas.what: Obstruction to extending a mixed extension over the generic point is the vanishing of a Z-valued (valuation) pairing (9.4.6.2)
Setup of ℓ-adic mixed extensions of pro-ℓ Barsotti–Tate groups with P multiplicative and Q étale
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic Tate modules with weight/monodromy filtration; ℓ-adic monodromy pairing

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX §9.4-9.5, apparently misfiled among the 1976 PD de Rham notes. All its content is published and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially accurate. 'sorite 9.3' is correct: the image shows a slightly garbled 'sorite' typed over.
The '432' at the bottom is the archive's page stamp, not part of the mathematical text.
